title: Fix ephemeral NAT context handoff causing DNS metadata staleness during Dedicated scale events
creator: Priya Singh
description: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent cross-tenant DNS resolution and stale DNS mappings after cluster scale-up/scale-down events. Investigation points to ephemeral NAT (SNAT) context handoff and connection tracking namespace reuse during autoscaler churn. This ticket tracks the production bugfix: prevent transient NAT/conntrack handoff from re-associating DNS UDP responses to the wrong tenant, add resolver metadata invalidation on route/peering swaps, and harden reconnection seams during scale events.
impact: High. Multiple enterprise Dedicated tenants observed domain lookups resolving to other tenants' hostnames for short windows after autoscaler events; customer escalations received from 3 major accounts and one SOC team. Potential data exposure vectored through DNS misassociation and request routing confusion.
customer_reports: Ticket #C-90812: acme-finance reported private hostname resolution to unrelated tenant after scheduled scale-down (replicated 3 times)
Ticket #C-91299: medapps observed transient 5xx errors and DNS CNAME responses with stale TTLs after peering maintenance
Support thread: #dedicated-tenant-isolation on Slack referenced by SE team
root_cause: During node drain/scale events the egress path for in-flight UDP DNS requests could be reassigned to a different SNAT context before conntrack entries and resolver metadata were invalidated. Two contributing factors: 1) ephemeral port ranges were re-used across tenant namespaces without deterministic socketmarking, and 2) route reparenting did not trigger immediate per-tenant resolver cache invalidation, allowing late-arriving DNS responses to be consumed by the wrong tenant proxy.
mitigation_applied: Hotfix deployed on 2026-03-07: conservative ephemeral port allocation increased to reduce reuse window
Temporary rule: block reparenting until in-flight conntrack entries drain for critical tenants (applied to cluster A)
Ops runbook updated to include immediate DNS cache flush for impacted tenants after scale events
code_changes: runtime: add socketmark tagging for tenant egress sockets to enforce namespace affinity
runtime: introduce deterministic ephemeral port allocator scoped per-tenant to prevent cross-tenant port collisions
control-plane: emit 'route-reparent' event to resolver service and trigger TTL metadata invalidation
infra_changes: kube: add drain-hook that waits for conntrack zero for tenant egress chain before reassigning node
networking: conntrack namespaces per-tenant enabled behind feature flag 'conntrack-isolation-v2'
monitoring: new metric 'tenant_dns_crossassoc' and dashboard panel in Console -> Dedicated -> Isolation
rollout_plan: Canary rollout across 3 Dedicated clusters: cluster-canary-1 (low-traffic), cluster-canary-2 (mixed), cluster-canary-3 (high-traffic). Steps: 1) enable feature flag in runtime on canaries, 2) deploy control-plane changes, 3) enable conntrack-isolation-v2 for 5 tenants on canaries, 4) run synthetic churn test (scale up/down 10x) and run prompt set of DNS queries, 5) monitor 'tenant_dns_crossassoc' and 'dns-response-latency' for regressions. If stable for 72h, progressive ramp to 25% of Dedicated fleet, then full roll after 7 days with no regressions.
acceptance_criteria: No customer-reported cross-tenant DNS associations after 1 week of rollout
tenant_dns_crossassoc == 0 for canary tenants during synthetic churn tests
DNS query success rate >= 99.95% and p95 latency regression < 10ms compared to baseline
Automated integration test added that simulates scale events and asserts no DNS response re-association
comments: 2026-03-06 - Priya Singh: Initial triage completed. Repro harness attached to canary cluster. Confirmed DNS responses occasionally arrive after route reparent and are matched to wrong tenant flow. Escalated to SRE for immediate mitigation.

2026-03-07 - Carlos Mendes: Deployed ephemeral port allocation increase and temporary blocking rule on cluster-canary-1. Observed reduction in reproductions from 7/day to 0-1/day for affected tenants.
2026-03-09 - Maria Alvarez (SRE): Captured conntrack dump showing entries with reassigned SNAT port IDs during node terminate. Proposed conntrack zero drain hook and socketmark enforcement.
2026-03-11 - Design review: UX team asked to add an incident annotation in Console release notes and a per-tenant isolation status indicator for Dedicated customers.
2026-03-14 - Carlos Mendes: Submitted PR #1286 for socketmark tagging and deterministic allocator. Need security review for socketmark KConfig change. Planning canary rollout starting 2026-03-15.
